takeaway: The left phrenic nerve pierces the central tendon. Phrenic (C3-5): motor and central sensation; lower six intercostals: peripheral sensation. T8 IVC, T10 oesophagus, T12 aorta.

lines.text: Which statement about the diaphragm is correct?
The book's answer: the left phrenic nerve pierces the central tendon.
The phrenic nerve, C3, 4 and 5, gives the motor supply and sensation to the central portion.
lines.say: The phrenic nerve, C three, four and five, gives the motor supply and sensation to the central portion.

lines.text: The lower six intercostal nerves supply sensation only to the periphery.
Now the levels. At T8: the right phrenic nerve and the inferior vena cava.
lines.say: (clears throat) Now the levels. At T eight: the right phrenic nerve and the inferior vena cava.

lines.text: At T10: the oesophagus and vagus. At T12: the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct.
lines.say: At T ten: the oesophagus and vagus. At T twelve: the aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct.

lines.text: So the IVC is not at T10, and the oesophageal hiatus is not at T12.
lines.say: So the inferior vena cava is not at T ten, and the oesophageal hiatus is not at T twelve.
